findings.title: Backup code plus any TOTP value skips the password
findings.body: Password verification runs only when credentials.totpCode is empty (if (user.password && !credentials.totpCode)). The new branch then accepts login whenever twoFactorEnabled is set and credentials.backupCode matches a stored code, and it never checks the TOTP value. A caller who knows only a backup code can send that code together with any non-empty totpCode and no password and receive a session. Backup codes are supposed to replace the authenticator, not the password, so this is a single-factor account takeover. Always verify the password on the backup-code path, and do not treat a present totpCode as proof that the password was already checked.

findings.title: Backup code match is case-sensitive and not normalized
findings.body: Stored codes are lowercase hex from randomBytes().toString("hex"), but the login (and the same indexOf in pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts) only strips "-" before comparing. Uppercase hex, spaces, or other separators from copy/paste or manual entry fail indexOf and are rejected as IncorrectBackupCode even when the code is correct. Normalize by removing non-alphanumerics and lowercasing before compare.

findings.title: Backup code consumption is not atomic
findings.body: The handler decrypts backupCodes, finds an index, then later writes the array back with that slot set to null. Two concurrent authorize calls can both read the same ciphertext, both see the code as unused, and both issue a session before either update lands. The code is therefore reusable under a race, contrary to the "exactly once" contract. Consume the code in a single conditional update (transaction or compare-and-swap on the encrypted blob) and only create the session if that update wins.

findings.title: Download control cannot start the file download
findings.body: The download action is a Button nested inside <a download href={backupCodesUrl}>. A click lands on the button, which does not activate the parent anchor, so the blob is never downloaded. The button also has no type="button" and no preventDefault, unlike the adjacent Close/Copy handlers, so if it sits in the enable form it will submit and call the enable API again with the previous TOTP code. Use a real anchor or a button that programmatically saves the blob, and keep it from submitting the form.

findings.title: Error tells users to generate backup codes in settings
findings.body: missing_backup_codes is "No backup codes found. Please generate them in your settings." Codes are only created inside TOTP setup and there is no settings action to generate or view them later. Users who enabled 2FA before this migration, or who dismissed the one-time display, are told to do something the UI cannot do. The copy should say they must disable and re-enable 2FA (with the authenticator) to obtain codes.

findings.title: 2FA e2e never proves a backup code can authenticate
findings.body: After OTP confirmation the UI now stops on the backup-code screen and does not call onEnable until Close. The enable-and-login test never dismisses that screen and still asserts the switch via locator.isChecked(), which is a Promise and is always truthy. The disable test only checks that a download filename and a toast appear. Nothing submits a backup code to credentials authorize or to the disable API, so the new login and one-time-consumption paths are untested. The file's own TODO notes this gap.
